interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log shows field manual-read route completion at 88% against a 95% target for Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, i.e. roughly 7 percentage points of routes were missed in that window. This is consistent with reduced manual read collection feeding more estimate substitution during the dispute-surge period, but says nothing about why completion fell short (e.g. staffing) or about response speed/CRM artifacts.

Authoritative CRM data confirms the stakeholder's framing that ticket volume roughly doubled starting August (590→1180) and remained elevated in September (1260), establishing the surge as a real volume phenomenon rather than a mere reporting artifact; it does not by itself indicate why bills are wrong.

This undercuts the 'response speed' component of CL-01's framing of the dispute surge as a speed problem; it says nothing about why bills are wrong.

Billing-db shows disputed bills split by read type: 1240 tied to ESTIMATED reads versus 1785 tied to ACTUAL reads, so a majority (about 59%) of disputed bills are associated with actual meter reads, not estimate substitution.

release_summary.summary: The stakeholder (SH-CS) originally framed the problem as a response-speed issue needing an AI auto-answer/auto-fix agent (CL-01), but the established problem (PD-1) is different: CRM dispute volume roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month since August (E-02), response times remain within SLA (E-03) so speed is not the driver, no tariff changes occurred (E-05, E-06), and disputed bills skew majority toward ACTUAL meter reads (1785) over ESTIMATED reads (1240) (E-04) - meaning the surge is primarily about something going wrong when processing real, non-estimated meter reads, not estimate substitution. Within contest scope, only one piece of this was actually resolved and released: a deterministic correlation of field route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95%, E-01) against the ESTIMATED-read dispute minority, which resolved unknown U-FIELD-READ-CONTRIBUTION-VALI. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds, because the critical question of what specifically causes the larger ACTUAL-read majority of disputes (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-MECHANISM) remains open and out of this release's scope, so it is released as a documented known limitation rather than blocking release entirely.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS) framed the surge as a response-speed/auto-fix problem; this framing was rejected (H-SPEED-AND-AUTOFIX REJECTED) based on E-01, E-03, E-04, E-07, since response times are within SLA (E-03) and the real driver is ACTUAL-read bill errors (E-04), not speed.

Field staffing shortfall (SH-FIELD claim E-07/CL-03) and AMI delivery degradation (H-AMI-DELIVERY) were both REJECTED as explanations for the dispute majority, contradicted by E-04 and E-12.

The only work item released (W-WI-1, status DONE) correlated route-completion shortfall (E-01, DA-ROUTE) against the ESTIMATED-read dispute minority (1240), resolving U-FIELD-READ-CONTRIBUTION-VALI; this is the full extent of the release_scope in solution_design (SD-1).

The critical unknown driving the larger ACTUAL-read majority (1785 disputes) - U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-MECHANISM / VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-MECHANISM - remains OPEN and outside this release's scope, so SC-ROOT-CAUSE-IDENTIFIED has not been met.
